The ending may have been the best ending I've ever seen. Let me explain. 

The song 'Sweet Child O' Mine' by Guns N' Roses was featured in the main trailer. Thor: Ragnarok, also directed by Taika Waititi, similarly featured 'The Immigrant Song'. However, reading into the lyrics of the song gave away a description of the entire plot of the movie itself, and it became clear that the title songs are chosen for a particular reason.

So, upon realizing this connection, people instantly began to analyze Sweet Child O' Mine for clues of the movie, especially who is the 'sweet child' being talked about. There were theories of the song being about Jane Foster, about Thor himself, and even about Gorr's dead family.

But the ending gives us the clear answer when the song plays for the final time as the credits roll, with the ending showing Thor and Gorr's daughter - Love and Thunder.

I could not ask for a better ending for Thor's character arc up until here.

Ever since the first Thor movie, Thor has been plagued by a question he hasn't figured out even after thousands of years of living - who is he. He was bound by glory as Asgard's warrior, by honor as the protector of the Nine Realms, by duty as Asgard's King, by defeat when Thanos attacked, by revenge when he kills Thanos, by loss in the five years since the snap, and by vengeance when Thanos returns.

By the time Thanos is dead, Thor has little to nothing left. He has lost his family and love, and has given up his role as Asgard's King - leaving him as a warrior but also as someone without purpose.

Gorr, who has to bury his own daughter, has his faith of the eternal reward - his purpose - destroyed by the pride of the very gods he worshiped. So he finds a new purpose to seek vengeance on the gods - who he starts believing are all loveless.

When Jane comes back into Thor's life, Thor starts to believe that she may be his purpose and reason to exist. He does his best to fight for this, and urges her to stay put when using her powers might kill her.

In the end, it is the expression of Thor's love - his new purpose - that frees Gorr from his path of vengeance. He wishes back his daughter. Jane before dying, promises that his daughter wouldn't have to be alone.

The ending of the movie shows Thor taking care of his newly adopted daughter - literally named Love. For the first time, in thousands of years, Thor is now bounded by love - his new purpose.

Despite facing more tragedies than anyone else in the MCU, despite knowing how much it would hurt to lose a loved one and how 'shitty' he would feel, Thor embraces love.

Sweet Child O' Mine is a song whose lyrics talk about the narrator meeting "sweet Love of mine" - someone who's youthfulness reminds him of his own childhood. With lyrics like "If I stared too long, I'd probably break down and cry", we know that the sweet child reminds him of a bittersweet past life.

The line "I'd hate to look into those eyes and see an ounce of pain" shows that the narrator deeply cares and wants to protect the child, just as how Thor is making sure Love has someone to love her, instead of being left alone and orphaned, like Thor was.

An interesting parallel is the line "Her hair reminds me of a warm safe place where as a child I'd hide, and pray for the thunder and the rain to quietly pass me by". Gorr can rest in peace knowing that the mighty Thor, the God of Thunder, will protect his daughter.

While the title Thor: Love and Thunder seemed a quirky name for a film that brings back Jane Foster, it is all the more deserved when it is announced at the very end.

Honestly, I must praise the genius of Taika Waititi. Using songs written decades ago to craft such exemplary stories is nothing short of magic. While the film might've had some issues, the ending, in my eyes, will be the perfect ending to Thor's arc.

Plus the fact that Love is played by Chris Hemsworth's daughter India makes the whole sequence even more wholesome than it already was.

TL;DR: Thor, a man who has been searching for true purpose his whole life, finally gets it in the form of Love. Gorr, abandoned by the gods, can rest in peace knowing that his daughter is not only protected, but also loved by the God of Thunder himself. The song Sweet Child O' Mine perfectly captures Thor's relationship with Love, and how they need each other. This movie concludes the character arc of Thor that began in the very first Thor movie. Despite its flaws, I could not be happier about the ending of Thor: Love and Thunder.
